summary: The note describes the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, also called the Brahmaputra Delta, Sunderbans Delta or Bengal Delta, a river delta in the Bengal region of South Asia shared by Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal. It is described as the world's largest delta, emptying into the Bay of Bengal, and as one of the most fertile regions in the world, earning the nickname The Green Delta. The note also gives its extent between the Hooghly and Meghna rivers and names its principal seaports.
one_line: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, the world's largest, is a fertile Bengal delta shared by Bangladesh and West Bengal, draining into the Bay of Bengal.
key_facts: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is also known as the Brahmaputra Delta, the Sunderbans Delta or the Bengal Delta.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is a river delta in the Bengal region of South Asia.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta consists of Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is described as the world's largest delta.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta empties into the Bay of Bengal.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is described as one of the most fertile regions in the world.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta earned the nickname The Green Delta because of its fertility.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta stretches from the Hooghly River on the west to the Meghna River on the east.
The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta is approximately 354 km (220 mi) across at the Bay of Bengal.
Kolkata in India is one of the principal seaports of the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta.
Mongla in Bangladesh is one of the principal seaports of the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta.
